subject: BlueQuill inference SLOs & throughput — plan and next steps
content:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sam Hart <sam.hart@bluequill.ai>
Cc: Maria Lopez <maria.lopez@bluequill.ai>
Date: Fri, 29 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: BlueQuill discovery follow-up — initial SLOs, constraints, next steps

Hi Sam / Maria —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps so we can align on a technical path and mutual action plan. I tried to keep this short and actionable.

Key pain points you shared
- Customer-facing personalization endpoints are missing sub-100ms median latency for short prompts, leading to visible UI stalls.
- Token-cost currently ballooning due to repeated full prompts; you need a caching/short-context strategy.
- Compliance: must keep user PII segregated and meet SOC2 evidence for procurement.

Goals we heard
- p50 inference latency target: <= 120ms for 32-token responses (median)
- p95 latency target: <= 400ms under expected burst (production)
- Sustained throughput: ~60 QPS for low-latency tier, with spikes to ~220 QPS during peak events
- Clear path to an on-prem/VPC deployment for regulated customers within 3 months of pilot

Initial technical notes / assumptions from Redwood
- Workload profile: primarily short prompts (avg 45 tokens in request, 70 tokens in response). If actual averages differ please share sample traces.
- Candidate model family: 13B-30B open-weights variants with quantized 4-bit runtimes for cost-sensitive paths; we can recommend smaller families for lower tail latency.
- KV / prefix caching: recommended to reduce repeated context re-encoding; expect 20-35% token cost reduction for repeatable contexts.
- Batching policy: continuous micro-batching tuned by latency SLO; we can tune target batch windows to meet p95 constraints.

Proposed topology options to evaluate in the technical deep-dive
1) Hosted Dedicated Pool (fastest time-to-value)
   - Dedicated GPU pool (mixed A100/RTX-class), pinned model variant, autoscale with burst nodes.
   - Redwood manages runtime, we provide SLA-backed SLOs + fallbacks to smaller variants.
2) Private VPC (production, regulated customers)
   - Customer VPC peering, private control plane, customer KMS, can run quantized variants on matched GPU fleet.
3) Hybrid (pilot on Hosted Dedicated -> migrate to Private)
   - Pilot for 4–6 weeks on Dedicated; migrate critical tenants to Private once SOC2 and performance profile validated.

Attachments attached: slo_runbook_v1.pdf (initial SLO mapping + test plan).

Immediate asks / next steps
- Sam / Maria: share 48–72 hour representative traffic export (timestamps, request sizes, QPS) and 10–50 sample prompts (anonymized).
- We will schedule a 60–75 minute technical deep-dive with our infra leads (Karthik Iyer, Marissa Cole) to walk topology options, runbook, and cost/latency trade-offs. Proposed window: Tue/Wed next week.
- We will prepare a short mutual action plan (MAP) and a one-week benchmark plan to measure p50/p95 vs. options.

If that looks right I’ll loop in Karthik/Marissa and propose times.

Thanks,
Tessa Morgan
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
https://redwoodinference.com/

From: Sam Hart <sam.hart@bluequill.ai>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sun, 31 May 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: BlueQuill discovery follow-up — initial SLOs, constraints, next steps

Thanks Tessa — this is very helpful and aligned. A couple clarifications from our side:
- The 60 QPS sustained is per-region (we currently have primary traffic on us-west but plan eu-west in Q4).
- Peak spikes are usually short (2–5 minutes) but can reach 200–250 QPS; we need burst handling without linear cost explosion.
- For compliance: we require SOC2 Type II evidence and a security questionnaire filled; Maria will open a procurement ticket with the team.

We’ll pull the anonymized traffic sample and 25 prompts (removing any user-identifying tokens) — expect those by EOD Tue.

We’re interested in both topology 1 and 3 (pilot -> private). Can you send a rough cost delta for Dedicated vs Private (range ballpark) ahead of the technical call? Also we’ll want to see a simple benchmark showing p95 behavior under realistic token sizes (30–120 combined tokens).

Sam Hart
VP Product, BlueQuill
sam.hart@bluequill.ai

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sam Hart <sam.hart@bluequill.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Maria Lopez <maria.lopez@bluequill.ai>
Date: Mon, 01 Jun 2026 08:43:00 -0700
Subject: Re: BlueQuill discovery follow-up — technical deep-dive & MAP prep

Appreciate the quick reply, Sam — looping in our infra and solutions leads to set up the deep-dive. Karthik and Marissa — brief background: BlueQuill (Sam/Maria) is targeting low-latency personalization endpoints, p50 ~120ms / p95 <=400ms, sustained 60 QPS per region with 200+ QPS spikes. They need an on-ramp to private/VPC within Q3 and SOC2 evidence for procurement.

Suggested agenda for the 75-minute deep-dive
- 0–10 min: quick context and success metrics (Sam)
- 10–30 min: workload profile walk-through (traffic samples + prompt examples)
- 30–55 min: topology & runtime options (Karthik) — hosted dedicated vs. private vs. hybrid; batching and KV cache strategy; quantization trade-offs
- 55–70 min: benchmark plan and acceptance criteria (Marissa) — p50/p95 measurement plan, test harness, dataset, and runbook responsibilities
- 70–75 min: immediate action items and scheduling MAP tasks

Topology notes (short)
- Tail-latency optimization: small dedicated pools for the low-latency tier, explicit reservation for hot paths, and fast-path model variants (smaller context windows + quantization).
- Burst handling: warm standby nodes + burst autoscaling with quick fallback to compat model variant to preserve SLA.
- Security: for VPC runs we support customer KMS + per-customer audit logging export; we’ll provide SOC2 artifacts and fill the questionnaire (see attached security_questionnaire_bluequill.xlsx).

Pre-call deliverables from Redwood (before deep-dive)
- Short SLO runbook + benchmark plan (attached: slo_runbook_v1.pdf)
- Topology sketch and a cost ballpark for Dedicated vs Private (we’ll share ranges in the meeting slides)

Please reply with 2–3 slots that work for BlueQuill next Tue/Wed (Jun 8/9). I’ll send a calendar invite with a short agenda and attach the MAP and runbook.

Tessa Morgan
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Thanks Tessa — Jun 8 at 10:00am PT or Jun 9 at 9:00am PT both work for us. We’ll share the anonymized traffic export and the sample prompts by EOD Wed (Jun 3).

Quick ask for the pre-meeting materials: can you include an example benchmark output (p50/p95) for a similar workload (short prompts, mixing 13B quantized and 30B quantized variants) so our engineering manager can validate expectations? Also please include a short checklist of SOC2 artifacts you’ll provide.

We’ll open a procurement ticket and attach the security questionnaire (I’ve added it to this thread). Looking forward to the deep-dive — appreciate the clear MAP approach.

Sam Hart
